cards.text: Friend, we're at Mount Sinai, back when the LORD spoke with Moses, Israel's leader. This is the account of Aaron and Moses, and it starts with the family of Aaron, Moses' brother. Four sons: Nadab the firstborn, then Abihu, Eleazar and Ithamar.

cards.question: Aaron's four sons are anointed and ordained to serve as ___.

cards.text: But this family has a hard chapter. Nadab and Abihu died in the presence of the LORD, out in the Wilderness of Sinai.

cards.question: What were Nadab and Abihu doing when they died before the LORD?
Nadab and Abihu left sons behind to serve as priests in their place.

cards.text: No sons. So while their father Aaron is alive, only Eleazar and Ithamar serve as priests.
Then the LORD tells Moses to bring the tribe of Levi and present them to Aaron the priest. A whole TRIBE, friend. Presented to ONE man.

cards.question: Moses presents the tribe of Levi to Aaron so they can take over the priesthood from him.

cards.text: The Levites will serve Aaron and the whole congregation in front of the Tent of Meeting. Aaron gets an entire tribe at once, and I'm over here inviting bakers one at a time. I'm not jealous. I'm a LITTLE jealous.

cards.question: Along with serving at the tabernacle, what will the Levites take care of?

answers.text: The furnishings of the Tent of Meeting
The flocks and herds of Israel

cards.text: The Levites are assigned to Aaron and his sons, given to him from among the Israelites. And Aaron and his sons carry out the duties of the priesthood.

cards.question: God says anyone in Israel is welcome to walk right up to the tabernacle.

cards.text: Then the LORD speaks to Moses again: "Behold, I have taken the Levites from among the children of Israel…" Taken them in place of somebody.

cards.question: The LORD says He took the Levites in place of every ___ Israelite.

cards.text: The Levites belong to Him, because all the firstborn are His. And He points back to one day in Egypt.

cards.question: What did the LORD do on that day in Egypt?

answers.text: Parted the waters of the sea

cards.question: On that day, the LORD set apart Israel's firstborn people but not their animals.

cards.text: Then in the Wilderness of Sinai, the LORD tells Moses to count the Levites by their families and clans.

cards.question: Which Levite males does the LORD tell Moses to count?

answers.text: Every male a month old or more

cards.text: And Moses counts them, just as the LORD commanded. A MONTH old, friend. That little guy can't hold his own head up, and he's already on the roster.

Levi's three sons are Gershon, Kohath and Merari, and each son's clans get counted, get a leader and get a side of the tabernacle to camp on. The Gershonites camp on the west and look after the tent, its covering and the curtains. The Kohathites camp on the south with the ark, the table, the lampstand and the altars, and the Merarites camp on the north with the frames, posts, tent pegs and ropes. Hey. Somebody's gotta bring the pegs.

cards.question: With the Levite clans on the west, south and north, where do Moses, Aaron and Aaron's sons camp?

answers.text: On the east toward the sunrise
On the west with the Gershonites

cards.text: Right in front of the Tent of Meeting, doing the duties of the sanctuary for the Israelites, and any outsider who approaches the sanctuary is to be put to death. Then the Levite total comes in: 22,000.
Now the LORD tells Moses to count every firstborn male of the Israelites, a month old or more, and list their names. The Levites will be the LORD's in place of all Israel's firstborn.

cards.question: The LORD also takes the Levites' livestock in place of the firstborn of the Israelites' livestock.
Moses counts the firstborn, just as the LORD commanded. Next to the 22,000 Levites, what does the firstborn count show?

cards.text: 22,273 firstborn. That's 273 more than the Levites. Friend, when I've got ONE extra cookie box and no baker to hand it to, I'm running laps around the bakery. Moses has 273.
The LORD speaks to Moses again: take the Levites in place of all the firstborn of Israel. And for the 273 extra firstborn, there's a way to redeem them.

cards.question: What's the price to redeem each of the 273 extra firstborn?
The LORD says the redemption money goes to ___ and his ___.

cards.text: So Moses collects 1,365 shekels from the firstborn, by the sanctuary shekel. Five times 273, right on the nose, and me, I lose count of chocolate chips at SEVEN.

cards.question: Moses gives the redemption money to Aaron and his sons, just as the LORD commanded him.

findings.problem: The opening identifies Aaron as Moses' brother and Moses as Israel's leader, but Numbers 3:1-2 does not state those facts and no supporting references are supplied for them.

rule.text: Facts from outside the passage are fine when they help, like who a new person is or who wrote a letter, with their reference.

findings.problem: This non-opening story card runs three sentences: the narration followed by "A whole TRIBE, friend." and "Presented to ONE man."

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: "That day in Egypt" depends on the preceding story card for its meaning. Standing alone, the question never identifies which day or event in Egypt it means.

rule.text: Always give context in the question. The story card before it isn't on screen anymore, so the question says who and what. Never "him," "that" or "it" pointing back to a card the baker can't see.

findings.problem: "On that day" again leaves the question without its own context. It should identify the day as the one when the LORD struck down Egypt's firstborn rather than pointing back to an unseen card.
